text: There is nothing so delicate as your moral character, and nothing which it is your interest so much to preserve pure. Should you be suspected of injustice, malignity, perfidy, lying, etc., all the parts and knowledge in the world will never procure you esteem, friendship, or respect.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter C, to his son, London, January 8, Old Style 1750
